answer: In a poll on the sable harbor's pulse, officials randomly audit submitted ballots, asking selected voters to appear with photo ID. They check IDs against a poll registry, counting audited ballots only for a matching, unused ID and rejecting failures; unaudited ballots are counted. An attacker risks a visit and another ID per audited alias. Audits can miss aliases, borrowed IDs can pass, and visits may exclude voters. The registry is an anchor, not proof of uniqueness.
